utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Di Fazio, Mr. Dutertre, are you ready to call your -- Mr. Dutertre, are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: We are, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would that be -- one second, please, Madam Usher. Would that be Faton Sefa?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has been provided with a consolidated witness statement of Faton Sefa and expects, at least that's what we are told, that this consolidated witness statement will be introduced as a Rule 73 ter statement. Now, it may be our printing facilities, but as you know we received these statements rather late so we can't comment on it any earlier. I see that photographs and sketches are inserted in the statement, which seems to be fine, to follow the statement. Mr. Dutertre, if I take you, for example, to what is page 6 in the printed-out hard copy for me, but perhaps first take you to page 5, paragraph 15 reads: "I previously made a sketch of the intake, see annex 3, U015-6853." And then it continues what markings were added, A, B, C, D, E, and F. Now, I look at page 6 where the sketch is inserted with the number, and I can't find any A, any B, any C, any D, any E, any F. So, therefore, I asked myself how to understand this document. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Yes, Your Honour. Those indications, A, B, C, D, E, F are in the original version in Albanian, which was communicated about a week ago, and you also have a translation, but on the translation, indeed, the manuscript signs are not there. So you need to use both versions; the version in Albanian and the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I now understand that it's not easy if you have just evening hours to read it to prepare yourself, then to find out that you have to consult the Albanian version. To be quite honest, on the sketch, I have difficulties to see what would be the difference between Albanian and English because it's just a drawing. But if you -- then I also noticed that sometimes on pictures which - but there could be a printing problem as well - in printing they appear very badly. And sometimes numbers cannot be seen anymore, so it is difficult. For example, page 14, I've got no idea that photograph. I may take it that these are the wooden filters, but numbers do not appear. Where usually the numbers appear in the right, top corner, I do not see any trace even of a number there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the reason why, Your Honour, I understand the problem. I annexed these to the Albanian version, the photographs which are in the text. So because of the problems we have for the printing, it would always be possible to look at the annex to see the document with the proper number. So for this page, number 14, if you look at annex 11 of the Albanian version, you will indeed see an enlargement of this photograph with the ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then I take it that we'll have a better opportunity to look at the annexes when they appear. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sefa. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. Perhaps, Madam Usher, I don't know whether the witness speaks any English, but otherwise headphones would -- do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I speak in English, but I didn't hear you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would prefer to speak and to listen in English rather than in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you accept that, I have a request. For when I say some of the terms, the technical terms, I can say in English, which for you is probably much better and for me it's very easy, very simple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you prefer to give your testimony --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I say it in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I invite you to put on your earphones, your headphones. Mr. Sefa, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sefa. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you are quite fluent in English as well. At the same time, if you would switch during your testimony too quickly from one language to the other, then it might be a problem for the interpreters because then they have to switch with you as well, unannounced, which might make matters rather difficult. So, therefore, I invite you to use one language; and if you use the other language, that is, English, to at least take your time so that the interpreters can switch together with you. Mr. Sefa, you'll first be examined by Mr. Dutertre, who is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Dutertre, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution will show the consolidated statement of Mr. Sefa according to 92 ter of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and, therefore, I have prepared a summary of the statement of Mr. Sefa, which I disclosed to the Defence, and I can read it out in the hearing when you deem it will be useful to do so. This statement of Mr. Sefa, following Rule 92 ter is a text signed in Albanian by the witness, and the annexes to this statement, and finally the translation in English. As for these three elements, I request number. I also disclosed yesterday to the Defence and the Chamber an index to the annexes of the statement, describing and giving their an ERN number, pages in the Albanian version and where they are mentioned, as well as the 65 ter number of the exhibits which have been given in January, in order to make things easier for the Chamber. The examination will be rather short with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, before we continue on the avenue of Rule 92 ter, will there be any objection to the use of 92 ter or to the statement? Mr. Harvey, you're the only one which I have not seen nodding either yes or no. No objection. Okay. Then please proceed, Mr. Dutertre, in the way you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to clarify one point. Do you wish me to read the summary of this 92 ter after having shown the statement to the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that what we first need is the attestation -- well, first of all, of course, to verify the personal data of the witness; then to have the witness attest, as required by Rule 92 ter; and then whether you read the summary at that moment or not is -- if it would be better for the understanding of the public to -- better for the understanding of the public for the remainder of the testimony, then you could read -- you could read the summary. If not, you could delay it to any other moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Sefa. I want to -- for your identity -- I want to check your identity. Your name is Faton Sefa. You are born on 23rd of May, 1954, in Gjakove, and you are Albanian. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: What is your present occupation, Mr. Sefa?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Unemployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, what was your last employment?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: First, I want to say hi to all of you and to explain briefly one. I started work in Hidrosistemi Radoniqi in 1982. I was a supervisor of the work there. In 1983, we started to fill the Radoniq Lake with water. In 1985, I became the manager for the maintenance of hydro-mechanical equipment. In 2002, I became the technical director of Radoniqi Hidrosistem Company. In August of 2006, I was dismissed from work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sefa. Do you recall, Mr. Sefa, having given a consolidated statement to the court in Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The last consolidated statement, you're asking me is that of 28th and 29th of May? In that case, it's true, I gave such a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you recall having signed that statement as well as all of the annexes?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. I have signed and agree with the content of the statements I've given. I'd like to inform the Trial Chamber that when I first started to give statements, even though initially I didn't know why it was to be used, the purpose was to provide technical information of the functioning of the Radoniqi Lake and things which occurred there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you. That was very clear. The -- you have been given a document. The usher has given you a document to your right-hand side which is the consolidated witness statement, along with the annexes signed on 28th, 29th May 2007. Oh, I'm sorry. I thought it had already been set beside you. Here is a binder which contains the document I've just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, I'm informed that you have other papers around as well, and the Chamber would very much like to know that if there's anything on your desk which is not provided by the Prosecution, the Chamber - I have no view of your table - we would like to know what it is and whether you have the intend to consult any of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that these are, perhaps, the personal copies you brought of the same statements. Would you please exclusively consult what you find now in the binder. If you would like to consult anything else, please ask permission to do so. Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Do you recognise -- sorry. There was a microphone problem. Mr. Sefa, do you recognise the document that's in this binder as being the consolidated statement you gave on May 28th, May 29th, 2007, along with the annexes in Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: This consolidated statement with the annexes, do they reflect what you would say if you were asked to testify today before the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: While making statements -- I would like to explain it better here. Your Honours, I want you to understand justly my statements. My aim was, as I previously stated, to provide technical information available to us and nothing else other than that. If you allow me, I would like to cite something from Gandhi. It's not a moral right of us to say things as we think they are about facts, reality that speak for itself, and thereof draw conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from what Gandhi said, Mr. Sefa, I would like to know whether the transcript of the statement you just recognised as the one you signed accurately reflects your declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I have stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so that's confirmed. And is that also what you would say if you were examined today on the same matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am willing to testify here, to go into more details, if you ask me, about the things I have stated in my statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's another matter. The only thing I would like to know is that if the same questions were put to you whether you would give the same answers, apart from whether there were any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are nodding no which is not totally understood by me. Would you give the same answers to those questions if they were put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see you nodding yes [Realtime transcript read in error "no"]. Could you please speak out loud because the interpreters cannot interpret your body language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre. Perhaps we should first assign numbers to the statements, because I take it that you want to have them admitted into evidence. Mr. Registrar, the consolidated witness statement of Faton Sefa and the attached 28 annexes --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be P367, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Dutertre, would you have a spare copy of the original so that the Chamber is in a position to use that as well? I just checked. I see that the new -- the index of the annexes with all the new numbers was sent to the Legal Officer yesterday, quarter past 6.00. I missed that -- I mean, I had left the premises already, so that's why I was struggling a bit yesterday evening. If at future occasions there would be a possibility, for example, to send it not later than 4.00 or 5.00, then I have less troubles. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. We will take care for that. I would also like to comment that in the transcript, line 19 on page 10 [as interpreted], I wonder whether there isn't a mistake where you asked -- I wonder whether there isn't a mistake where you asked -- I wonder whether there isn't a mistake where you said: "I see you nodding no," whereas, I believe you mean yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I saw, as a matter of fact, the head of the witness moving initially from left to right rather than up and down, so therefore that's what I interpreted as nodding no, but this has now been clarified. When you referred to page 10, line 19, Mr. Dutertre, we were only at page 10, line 17, so a reference to a line still to come was not entirely clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note, Your Honours, that the Albanians have their own way of saying no and yes when they nod.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what, as a matter of fact, Judge Hoepfel told me as well, that the nodding horizontally rather than vertically should be understood not in the way we would understand this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Well, have we given an exhibit number to the summary statement -- the consolidated statement and what would that be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's just been done. P367 [Realtime transcript read in error "P267"], Mr. Dutertre. I may have not been clear. Was it -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether I misspoke when I intended to refer to P367 because that's what the number is, although it appears on page 11, line 11, as "P267." Please proceed, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. At this stage, I would like to read out the summary if there are no objections. That is the 92 ter summary statement which has been sent out yesterday and which is a summary of the consolidated statement given by Mr. Faton Sefa, which is now P367. [In English] "Mr. Faton Sefa gained a university diploma in mechanic engineering in 1977. In 1982, he started working with the Hidrosistemi Radoniqi Company, eventually becoming technical manager. In 2006, he left the company. "Hidrosistemi Radoniqi controls and maintains the Lake Radonjic canal. Mr. Sefa was part of a project to create the Lake Radonjic reservoir, which was completed in 1983 and became functional in 1985. It supplied drinking water and irrigation water to the residents of Djakovica/Gjakove and Orahovac/Rahovec. "Mr. Sefa describes how the water-supply system consists of a water intake located in the village Lluka e Eperme, the Lake Radonjic canal which conducts water from the intake in Lluka e Eperme to the north-west side of Lake Radonjic, the Lake Radonjic reservoir itself, an outlet point located at the south-eastern part of Lake Radonjic, and a water-treatment plant and a distribution network. "Mr. Sefa explains how the intake at Lluka e Eperme consists of two gates which, when closed, divert water into the Lake Radonjic canal. A further three pairs of gates control the flow of water at the beginning of the Lake Radonjic canal. However, between 1995 and 2003, these three pairs of gates were kept open so that, in fact, only the first two gates controlled the flow of water. "Before the flow of water reaches the three pairs of gates, however, there are steel protection grilles with five centimetre openings. Thus, any object larger than five centimetres cannot pass through the gates into the Lake Radonjic canal. Mr. Sefa says that the grilles were in place for many years before the conflict started and were still in place and not showing any signs of damage when he revisited the canal in October/November 1999. "Wooden filters were also located after the three pairs of gates, in the direction of the canal, and had been in place for many years before the conflict started. "Mr. Sefa describes how the water was collected throughout the year, except for July and August. He learnt that from May or June 1998, no staff were present at the intake. "Mr. Sefa describes the Lake Radonjic concrete canal, which begins in the village of Upper Lluka and passes by the villages of Lluka e Eperme, Irzniq, and through the village of Kodralija. The concrete canal is seven kilometres in length and the average rate of water-flow is between two to three cubic metres per second. The concrete canal has 42 cascades, designed to break the force of the water-flow as it drops some 70 metres from start to finish. The force of the water is such, however, that objects dropped into the canal are normally forced down its length. "Daily monitoring of the canal is undertaken and reports of any debris are acted upon and the canal cleaned. This monitoring and cleaning stopped, however, from around June 1998, during the conflict, and did not resume until around June 1999. The KLA had control of this area from March 1998, and it was difficult for the staff of Hidrosistemi Radoniqi to enter the Decani area since the use of company vehicles might attract fire from the KLA. "Normally, the canal was also cleaned annually, but this did not occur in 1998 due to the war. "Mr. Sefa explains that near the village of Irzniq, an area of the canal was overgrown with trees, plants, and bushes, which had grown in soil accumulated in the basin of the canal, and this undergrowth affected the water-flow which was always very slow. This area was not cleaned at all between 1985 and 2002. This overgrowth was an obstacle. Mr. Sefa is not sure whether human bodies could pass through this part of the canal in 1998. "When Mr. Sefa visited this area in 2002, he observed extensive vegetation and debris. Some trees appeared to be up to 18 years old. The area was extensively cleaned for the first time in 2002 and seven lorry-loads of debris were removed. "Mr. Sefa states that between the end of the concrete canal and the water's entry into the lake, there is a natural canyon through which the water flows. "Mr. Sefa describes how the lake has a surface area of around 540 hectares and is 60 metres at its deepest pointed. Objects cannot float against the water-flow up the canal. "At the outlet from the lake, the water is treated at the water-treatment plant before going into the distribution network. Mr. Sefa explains that, during the war, Serbian forces controlled the southern banks of the lake and that the lake represented a natural border between Serbian and KLA forces. Mr. Sefa performed some work at the outlet during the conflict and under the observation of MUP forces. "Mr. Sefa recalls that Serbian police discovered bodies and human remains at the canal, but did not visit the site. He says that no human remains were found at the canal during the first cleaning after the war in 2001." [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I've finished the reading of this summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two very brief comments, if I may. First of all, I forebear from raising the issue of those aspects of this witness's testimony where opinion evidence is expressed without the necessary qualifications, and there are one or two areas where that occurs. That is an issue which Your Honour's indicated in the past is a matter that can be dealt with separately by way of submission. I therefore don't take issue at this stage. Secondly, though, simply for the sake of accuracy, the summary that has just been read out contains, at paragraph 9, the suggestion that this witness's statement involves an assertion of KLA control of the canal from March 1998. And Your Honours will have seen from paragraph 82 of the witness statement that the witness was able to give certain positions of Serb troops in the area around the lake, but specifically indicated regarding Irzniq and up to Lluka e Eperme, that he did not know during the relevant period who was or which side was in control of those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, would you agree with Mr. Emmerson? Would you not agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I sent in this document last evening, and, indeed, I will submit to any of the comments made by the Defence. As regards the comments regarding paragraph 82, indeed, that paragraph refers to Irzniq and the intake at Lluka e Eperme, and the text states that the witness does not know exactly who controlled, who was in charge, of those towns, but there's no precise date mentioned; whereas, there is a reference to annex 26 with a diagram, which does indicate the positions of the Serb forces in the region, which makes it possible to understand both the consolidated statement, the resume given by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the point is that pointing at certain positions held by whatever party in itself does not yet allow for conclusions as who was in control.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think I can -- if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's -- and apart from that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's not the evidence. The evidence is in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: An assertion of a positive is not an assertion at the absence of a negative, given that the witness himself has said that an area is not marked on his map. He is unaware of who is in control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, keeping in mind the function that it should give as good as possible to the public an impression of what to find in the statement that the matter has been sufficiently dealt with. Meanwhile, Mr. Dutertre, I now have in front of me the original version. You earlier said, Look at the original version and you'll find the explanations. May I take you to paragraph 15, for example. In the original, it says: "I previously made a sketch of the intake, see annex 3. On this sketch inserted below, I added the following markings ..." Now, I noticed that annex 3, the number has been changed for whatever reason. The number U0156853 has been stricken out. It is now annex B. Then in the text of the statement itself, where this is inserted, the number is taken out with some red pen. I do not know why the number is taken out and replaced by either initials or another number, 42. That's unclear to me. Therefore, the annex 3 seems not to be exactly the same as what we find annotated in the statement itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness gave a first testimony -- well, there was several. There was one where he made the sketch, he drew the sketch, that is included in annex 3 which at the time was called annex B of that first hearing, that first testimony -- statement. And the number was U0156853. That was annexed to the consolidated statement and the entire statement was modified, and, therefore, that's why that number was crossed out and replaced by another number. And that is why we gave you the index which enables you to cross-reference these documents. As regards the A, B, C, D, E, and F, these letters are to be found on the sketch, as you will find it in the Albanian version so that you have the sketch from the previous statement which is included in the annex with a changed ERN number; and under paragraph 15, you have the same sketch with additional markings made by the witness for the purposes of the consolidated statement. I hope I was clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I understand that the stricken-out number, therefore, now is replaced by the new number on the top of annex 3, last two digits 87.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true. Exactly. The same applies to all of the annexes. The ERN numbers have been crossed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I now see that. And now the -- so we have now two follow-up versions of U0156853. That is the one which has now become -- which used to be annex B but is now annex 3 with a new ERN number 87; and inserted in the statement, we find the original U0156853, but now with the markings made. So, as a matter of fact, we find part of the sketches, exhibits, as annexes and other versions with markings as part of the statement itself. Now, it's slowly clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's exactly correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For your -- probably for your much better to understand that. In your -- in annex 27 ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 27 -- [In English] In annex 27, you have exactly -- you have exactly description when there was Serbian forces. I make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a matter which is purely of a procedural nature, and there's no need at this moment to come back to that. The only -- one of the things you don't have to bother about is how the summary of your statement was drafted. Your statement in this respect seems to be perfectly clear. It's just how it is brought to the public that was of some concern, not the statement itself. Mr. Dutertre, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. To come back to the issue of who was controlling the area, if you look at paragraph 45, there is mention of that. But for your information and for reference, control as of March 1998 was not something that was discussed here. In fact, as regards the remainder, I have very few questions for the witness because we have admitted the statement under Article 73 ter; and for reasons of timing that we're all familiar with, I would simply like to put one question to the witness, which is as follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, you have indicated that the various intakes, the gates and the canal and the lake and then the water-treatment plant, this whole system was aimed at providing irrigation and also providing drinking water to the inhabitants of the region. Could you tell us exactly which towns received drinking water from this system; that is, the water that came from the Bistrica River.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: If you look at the annex 27, there is a map, 0163281. In that map I have shown where the military and police forces had been stationed, I mean the Yugoslav military and police forces. The question why I did not say where the KLA forces were or whether there were any KLA forces, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [No interpretation] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not to further respond on the matter, but just to tell the Court what towns received drinking water from this system.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to come to that. I just wanted to explain first how I knew that there were Serb forces in the area, because we went to those areas to check whether there was water supplied to the areas or not. Then Bitesh, Dubrica, Novo Sello, Ferija - these are the places that received water - Palabardhi, Supoti, Janosh, Cermjan, Netici, Beci. And if you are interested only in the area around the lake, these are the villages around the lake, but there are 72 villages all in all that are supplied with water from this system. Because we went to these areas to see whether water was supplied or not or whether there was an explosion or not, I could see the Serb forces and I had information that there were military and police forces in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, was the town of Gjakove provided with drinking water through this irrigation system coming from Bistrica, the water having been treated at the south-eastern corner of the lake, the Radonjic Lake?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The hydro system worked during all the time, before the war and after the war, with the exception of three days when NATO bombed and there was damage to the system. This was in May 1999 when there was not any supply for three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: But, in fact, my question was more precise than that. Was the city of Gjakove -- did the city of Gjakove receive water from the water-treatment plant and does it still receive water; that is, from the south-eastern corner of the lake which was part of the entire water system, the Hidrosistemi?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have, perhaps, a very small question. Mr. Sefa, we previously were provided with maps in this case where apparently a river appears, which might be the same river as Bistrica river, but which is called Decanska Bistrica. Is that the same? Because in the Albanian original, the name of the river is the different from what we see on this map, although logic tells me that, most likely, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Decanska Bistrica is a Serb word or term. It's the same river, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand. I thought "Decanska" might stand for something related to Decan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Because it passes by Decan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So where in Albanian it says "River Bishtrica," in the Serb language it says something like "Decana Bistrica"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are several rivers that are called Bishtrica. In Albanian, the real word in Albanian is Lumi i Bardhe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that even further complicates it, but it is the same river, as far as I understand. That was most important to me. Which Defence counsel will be first to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, who's counsel for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, may I start, please, by asking you some questions to clarify your own movements during 1998 and thereafter. Now, first of all, did you personally have any responsibilities at the Lake Radoniq area itself between the beginning of 1998 and September 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In the beginning of 1998, we were ordered to take care of the maintenance of the mechanical equipment. I was responsible for that, and it's also written in the statement. It's in point 44, paragraph 44, it says there who was responsible for the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. What I'm trying to understand, Mr. Sefa, is your own physical movements during the period of 1998, where it was you personally went, how often you visited the different parts of the water system between Lluka e Eperme and the lake itself. So if we can start with the lake itself, did you personally visit the Lake Radoniq area itself during 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I went to Lluka e Eperme in March 1998. I did not go to the precise intake point area until 1999. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy for you to start at the other end of the water system if you want, but let's be systematic about it. Did you personally ever visit the water intake system, that is to say, I'll call it the dam at Lluka e Eperme, at any time during 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In February/March 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because just a moment ago, I thought you said you didn't go to the precise intake point until 1999. Are we speaking at cross-purposes here?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No. I went to the intake point once in 1998, and you have that in my statement, but I -- this was in February/March 1998. Later I did not go. I was supposed to go in August 1998 in order to stop the water when there was talk about some bodies,; but at that time, we went to a local Serb and he went there to stop the water. So myself and my colleague, when we went there, we told him, "It's good that we don't need to go and stop the water ourselves." So we went to Decan, but we did not go to the precise point, intake point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, I've got quite a lot of questions for you, so if you could try to focus your answers as much as possible to the question. I've understood your evidence to be one visit to the dam at Lluka e Eperme during 1998, and that visit took place in February or March. Is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: February --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- or March, I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've just mentioned an occasion in August when you thought you might have to go and change the flow of the water, to stop the water, but in fact a local Serb went there. Just so that we're clear and there's no confusion about that, the incident that you're there referring to is an incident that took place in September, on or about the 9th of September to be precise, during the Serbian investigation of a series of bodies that were recorded as having been found in the canal area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't remember the date, but the exact thing is that we did not go on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just wanted to be clear that it wasn't in August. So that deals with Lluka e Eperme. During 1998 now, focusing on that year, did you yourself at any point visit any section of the canal at any point between Lluka e Eperme and the lake?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Third question then in the sequence of the water system. Did you yourself visit the lake during 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In 1998, the dam part of the lake, yes, the southern part of the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, just to avoid confusion, when you refer to the dam part, you're not referring to Lluka e Eperme, but to the dam at the southern end of the lake. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So when was the first time after 1998 that you ever personally visited any section of the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date. I think it is in my statement. It could have been October, November, December 1999; however, it is in my statement. We visited only the Lluka e Eperme area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So as far as you can recall - let's just be as clear as we can - as far as you can now, recall the next time you visited any section of the canal would have been after the war was over?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The rest of the canal I visited after the war ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm sorry, because there's again, I'm afraid, some confusion in your answer. You've told us that some time around October, November, or December 1999, you visited only the Lluka e Eperme area. So let's just deal with that. Was that the first part of the canal that you visited in 1999?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: These things are written in my statement, and I wanted to explain. We are speaking about a canal that is seven kilometres long, and I visited the entry part, the intake part, of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's very helpful, Mr. Sefa. If you could just listen to the question, because otherwise we're going to take a lot of time on unnecessary information. So just listen very carefully to the question. The next time that you visited any section of the canal you've told us, is this correct, was after the war, when you went to the dam at Lluka e Eperme. Is that right? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And was it at some point after that visit that you first visited any section of the canal between the dam and the lake?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In the year 2001, I can't remember exactly when, we visited the last part of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. That -- and when you say "the last part," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I wanted to explain something here. We call canal the part that is concrete; the rest of it is a canyon. There is erosion there and the water-flow is very rapid. There is silt and sediment in the area because of the energy of the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So that we're clear, are you saying that in 2001, you visited the area where the concrete section ends and the natural canyon begins? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you remember whether you visited any other part of the canal at any time in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the first time you ever went to the area in the canal around Irzniq was in 2002. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please, the witness can answer I think.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said "the first time," and you mean by this before the war or after the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first time since the war began.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Well, this was after the war anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Dutertre, you were on your feet. You didn't raise any objection against the question at that moment, so I was a bit uncertain about what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't want to interrupt my colleague. Just a point of clarification on the question which was asked at the line 13: [In English] "And can you remember whether you visited any other part of the canal at any time in 2001?" [Interpretation] The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just a clarification I was seeking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand the point. I'll deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And thank you for raising it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be absolutely clear, I sorry to ask you the same question again, Mr. Sefa. But just to be absolutely clear, during 2001 you've told us that in the back end of the year, you visited the dam at Lluka e Eperme; and I then asked you whether you could remember if you visited any other part of the canal in 2001, and you said no. And what Mr. Dutertre is asking is did you mean, "No, I can't remember," or did you mean, "No, I did not visit any other part of the canal in 2001?"

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In 2001, I went to visit the last part of the canal and the first part of the canal, but not the part that you mentioned in Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So if we can get your testimony absolutely clear. In 2001, you visited two parts of the canal: The dam at Lluka e Eperme and the area where the concrete section of the canal stops and the natural canyon begins. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were both of those visits after the war had ended?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So were these both in the autumn period?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And then just to return to the area adjacent to Irzniq, or Rznic, rather, your first visit to that area, after the war had begun, was in 2002, was it not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, I think you tell us, in your statement, you hadn't been to that area at any time for the decade between 1992 and 2002. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just before we take a break, can I be clear, when you went there in 2002, to that area adjacent to Irzniq, was there a recovery or cleaning operation then taking place when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: During this period, the Radoniqi company was managed by internationals, and they ordered to clean the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: And during that time, they had the responsibility for anything that was done there. They commissioned a firm to do the job, and they also supervised the works.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. That doesn't answer my question, but may I just ask a supplementary question in relation to your answer and then come back to the question I asked you. What was the name of the independent contractor, the independent company, that they employed?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Fidani-l.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can I ask you, did the Clevery Consulting company have anything to do with that operation or not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: What firm? Could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Clevery Consulting Limited, nothing to do with that operation?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The first time I hear this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's helpful. When you arrived in 2002 to that area, was the cleaning-up operation already underway at the time that you got there?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: It had already started, but it had not finished yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So some of the debris had been removed, but some was still there?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, finally, can I just ask you to confirm this. Are you aware that after the war had ended, as people in the villages were reconstructing their houses, many used the canal as a dumping-ground for silt and debris from the reconstruction process?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: That's true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so the essential position is this, I think you can confirm, you are not in a position to help us at all about the state of any bushes or trees in the canal at that area close to Irzniq during 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Well, frankly, I can't say whether it was like this or like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Emmerson. We will have a break, Mr. Sefa, and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, could we have a look, please, at annex 27 to your witness statement, which you were going to give an explanation for a little earlier. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to does you some questions just to establish what you do and don't know exactly about Serbian deployments in the canal area at both ends. Now, you've said in your statement, at paragraph 82, that as regards Irzniq, you don't know who was in control of Irzniq at any given time, so I'm not going to ask you questions about that section of the canal. But can I ask you just to look at annex 27 for a moment, and you've drawn there a series of crosses with the word "Serb" at the bottom. So do we understand it to be your recollection that there were Serb forces deployed in the area which you have marked those crosses as appearing in?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already explained it to you, but I'm repeating it, that every cross indicates the position of the Serb police and military forces. Because I couldn't have access to that place, I didn't mark the locations of the KLA because I had no information on that. What I know was based on hearsay. I didn't have anything to do with them until then, that's why I don't know anything about that. I'm not sure about Irzniq either, where they were, how many there were, and so on. This I've stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that clarification because there are aspects of some of the language in your statement which may suggest that you were clear that there was a front line, as it's described I think at one point, between the KLA and the Serbs at the northern end of the lake. And if what you're telling us now is that you don't know exactly where the KLA forces were deploying or what areas of territory they were controlling at any one time, then the term "front line" may be a bit of a misnomer. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: It happened often for me to go and intervene in the course of work in the dam at Radoniq Lake where the water treatment is made at the southern part, and from there I could see large artillery forces with all sorts of equipment, tanks, and so on. And when we happened to go to nearby villages, they fired from the hill of Tesh [as interpreted]. That's why I couldn't go any further than that. It was an unpleasant situation and we were afraid that they might kill us, hearing that we were couriers of the KLA. That's why we were afraid to go, to venture any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The transcript is recorded as you referring to "the hill of Tesh." Can I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Bitesh.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Suka Bitesh, that is the elevated position sometimes called Suka Radonjic in Serbian. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Suka Radoniqit is another from Suka Bitesh. By the word "Suke," we referred to the top of the hill. [In English] It's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were you able to see the Serb police or military deployed at ground level, as well, during your visits?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, we did, because we had to go there among them. I was obliged to work in their vicinity, and I could see them with my own eyes. To this day you could see traces of the previous fortifications or trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know if they were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Until now, the Suka Bitesh and Suka Radoniq have been at least described as identical --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- So the answer the witness just gave certainly needs further --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I was going to use his plan, if I may, just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- establish what he was referring to by Suka Bitesh. May I just pursue the last answer for just a moment or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you able to tell, during your visits, whether the troops that were deployed on the ground were patrolling the area?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Once I remember that we went to Bitesh hill and they didn't allow us to proceed further. And when we descended the hill, we saw them firing from Biteshi hill. I can't say for sure whether they were deployed at the foot of the hill, but on the top, yes, there were police and military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, the question I'm asking you - and if you can't help us one way or the other, then that's perfectly understandable because you were visiting from time to time - but I simply want to know whether during your visits, you ever observed Serb MUP units or military units moving only the ground; that is, not on the hill, but deployed, patrolling on the ground, coming and going?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I saw only from Gjakove and Osikhila, which is a village in the direction of Gjakove, Decan. It's the first village when you leave on the way from Peje to Gjakove. There I saw a large number of people. There was a large convoy with over 40 vehicles, armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we take it this -- put it this way and see if you agree with this proposition. From what you yourself observed, from your own observations, you don't know one way or the other whether the Serb troops were penetrating north on the ground from time to time towards the canal area?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. But if you refer to the map, a military map, you can see that the lake is at the quota of 456 above the sea level. They were stationed at an elevation which was 500, 550 metres above the sea level, which gives you the idea that from that elevation you can have an overlooking view of the entire territory around the lake. Since we visited that place, you may understand that we see the position or the positions they were firing from.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: This is what I can say about that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we just look at your map, annex 27. The ring -- or the line of crosses, if we look at the upper-most cross on the map on the left-hand side, immediately adjacent to that is a circle by the shore of the lake with the word "Bitesh" written beneath it. What is that representing?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: This is Suka e Biteshit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are saying from this map, are you, that there were Serb forces on Suka Bitesh itself?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And across to the left of that, what does that tell us on your map?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: On the left, there is Suka e Baballoqit. It is a hill over Hereq, where there used to be a colony of Serbs and Montenegrins who, in order to be protected, were helped by some Serbian forces. We saw the smoke coming out of the artillery explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Fine. And that's what the cross to the left on your map is intended to indicate? Can you just have a look at the map, Mr. Sefa, while you're answering the question because there seems to be a circle immediately above that cross, another circle, and I wonder what that circle indicated.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: By this I wanted to indicate that Baballoq is located there, the village of Baballoq --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- and that this is the road Gjakove-Decan and approximately the place where they were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. Again, help us -- sorry. Did you want to add something?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] If you give me the chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, please.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Suka Cermjan is higher than the other two, Bitesh and Radoniq hills. They are adjacent to one another, but they are higher. And from this position, if you look at the right side of the lake, there are no forces, at least I didn't know that there were forces belonging either to the Serbs or to the KLA because it's a terrain you can see clearly from that point. For the upper part, in the direction of Ratishe, I couldn't see anything because I didn't have any instruments to observe it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's very helpful. So that you know, Mr. Sefa, we've heard testimony in this court to the effect that not only were Serb forces stationed on Suka Cermjan but that there were military engagements between the KLA and the Serbs around Suka Cermjan. So that we understand your testimony, are you saying you know positively that there were not or merely that you never, yourself, observed them; or you don't know one way or the other; or what is it you're trying to tell us about Suka Cermjan?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: If you look at the map, there's another map that corresponds to this. It's a topographical map. You can see between Suke of Cermjan and Radoniq, there is a road that leads to remote villages in the direction of Rakoc. Since there were Serb forces deployed there on the other side, where there is now an Italian airport, you can have a look at the entire zone because it is of a higher position. So from there we could observe the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you another way, Mr. Sefa. How many times during the period from March to September 1998 did you personally go to the lake?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: From March to September 1998, on this part of the lake, I went almost every two or three days, at least two times every week.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And which part of the lake are you there referring to?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I meant the part where I have indicated the crosses, where I put the crosses, where we went at least once a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you help us about this, and again if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you please invite the witness to tell us exactly what locations he visited, because if he says --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- "I went where the crosses are," Baballoq is on this sketch even north from the most northerly part of Lake Radonjic, which certainly does not correspond --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with what we find on --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- I take Your Honour's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just -- in answer to the Judge's question, could you just explain precisely which specific parts of the lake that you were visiting on those occasions. And it may be easier for you to do it by reference to the facility, the water-treatment area, or whichever part of the facility it was that you were personally visiting.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. The filtering station we visited regularly, every week, which is on the road to Suka Radoniqit and Cermjan, on a lower position. From there, you can see Biteshi hill from the main road, and the villages of upper Novo Sello, Janosh, Sopot. Every week we went there once or even more sometimes, but at least once. I understand that the owner wanted to ask about the northern part. This part we could observe from a distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So it was the filtering station that you regularly visited. Did you visit any other facility, or was it just the filtering station?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: We went also to Rahovec --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- but we are talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was an ill-phrased question. At Lake Radoniq was there any other part of the water facilities that you visited on a regular basis, or was it just the filtering station that you were visiting?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. There is the outlet of the tunnel we -- from where we let the water go out to irrigate the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And are both the filtering station and the outlet of the tunnel, are both of those locations in the south end of the lake? No?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, in the southern part, but they are not close to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it's from those two locations in the southern part that you're basing your information about the deployment of Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, finally, can I ask you this --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Can I? [Interpretation] In the vicinity of the dam, there is a place where the alarm system is. In case the water would overflow the dam, there was an alarm system, and it was the place where the police and military forces used to sleep. From there, you can observe the entire surrounding terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And, again, to avoid any confusion, when you're referring to the dam in that answer, you are referring to the dam at Lake Radoniq rather than the dam at Lluka e Eperme. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: We call dam this part, and that we use another word which I don't know how to say in English. It's a similar word. But an Albanian word "kaptazh."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am sorry. Did --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Intake. For this area we said intake, and dam we said for the Radoniq Lake. That is different completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. It is, I think, difficult for the interpreters if you switch between English and Albanian in the middle of an answer, and I'm afraid that that answer got a little bit lost?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that when the witness used the word that was translated "dam," that was at the end of the lake where water was stopped; whereas, as far as I remember, he at least did not usually use the word "dam" for what was the intake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think that may be me that uses dam for Lluka e Eperme.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. That's helpful. One final question about the area around the lake and the canal, if I may. And, again, please don't hazard a guess if you don't know the answer to this. But the can you confirm that on either side of the canal runs a dirt track from the lake going in a north-westerly direction along the canal and parallel to it?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Excuse me. Can you repeat again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. From the canal -- I'm sorry. From the lake, going in a north-easterly direction, along the natural part of the channel, there are dirt tracks passable by rough-terrain vehicles --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a mistake? I always got the impression that it goes north-westerly direction, if you start --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour is quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Starting point, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Starting --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- point is the point at which the canal enters the lake; and then proceeding in a north-westerly direction - His Honour corrects me - there are dirt tracks either side and parallel to the canyon, which are passable by rough-terrain vehicles. Can you confirm that, please?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Depends. In difficult conditions, it's impossible to drive, even four-wheel drives.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We, obviously, have some aerial photographs of the area along the canal which show - I don't think they're very clear on your black-and-white copies, without pulling them up for you - which show dirt tracks running along, first of all, the eastern side from the lake up the natural section of the canal and on the western side as well. Now, are you saying that those dirt tracks were, at times, not passable?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness called what you called the natural section "the canyon."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The canyon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- use the same words as consistently as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no road at all in the part of the canyon. Up to the beginning of the canyon, there is an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not speaking of asphalt roads.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] No, no, no. It's a bad road. [Interpretation] It's an ordinary road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll just see if we can pull up a photograph. In the meantime, I'll move on to another topic and come back to that, if I may, whilst that's being identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me ask you some questions, if I may, please, about your understanding of the way in which the intake at Lluka e Eperme was controlled. First of all, Sali Zejnaj is an employee whose primary responsibility was control of the intake at Lluka e Eperme, is that correct, in 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The person who was responsible for the intake in Decan was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'm going to come back to him. It's Musli Mulliqi, is it?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he worked alongside Sali Zejnaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Sali Zejnaj was based at the intake position at Lluka e Eperme. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Now and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say "now and again." In addition to that, was he responsible for patrolling along the canal area?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. He did that now and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, you -- you've used that expression "now and again." Apart from those two responsibilities, that is, manning the intake and patrolling the canal, did he have other responsibilities as well during 1998 or were they his jobs?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I am saying "now and again" because he did patrol the area when he had a possibility, and this went on until June of 1998, when he was driven out of his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's what I wanted to come to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst I do, could we please pull up P45 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Prior to June 1998, were you in contact with Sali Zejnaj on a regular basis or not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No. Only when I mentioned it in my statement. It was in March when I met him for the last time before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So when was the next time after March that you met him?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: After 1999, I don't remember when I met him. I didn't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you aware - and yes or no at this point will do - were you aware that it was Sali Zejnaj's practice to leave the gates open at Lluka e Eperme, in order to lower the level of the water in the River Bishtrica so that civilians could escape from the Serbs? Did you know that he was manipulating the water up until June in order to enable civilians to escape across the river bed at the River Bishtrica?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Allow me to give an explanation here. Sali was an employer of mine. It was not that we had direct supervisory relationship. At that time I was not his boss, let's say his manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm simply asking you the question: Were you aware, yes or no, that he used to deliberately manipulate the water by leaving the gates at the intake open in order to ensure that the level of the water in the River Bishtrica was kept to a minimum so that civilians could flee across it? Was that something that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: And, second, if he was given an order, I want to remind you of the fact that the director of the company at that time was a Serb. Maybe he was given the order and he had to but comply with it, but I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll come to that in a moment or two. Whilst we do, you can see the photograph on the screen in front of you. So we're now looking along the canal towards the lake. You can't see the lake in the orientation that we've got at the moment. Perhaps if we look to the top of the screen you can see the lake in the distance, and you can see the area that you're looking at is the end of the concrete section and the start of the canyon. Do you see on the left-hand side of the photograph the dirt track that appears to run parallel to the water? Can you see that? Yes?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That dirt track was there in 1998, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember this track.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, you've told us that you didn't go to any section of the canyon or canal during 1998. Are you saying that you remember that it was not there at some previous time? What exactly are -- is your evidence on this?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I can only say that I have never been on this track.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And, again, we see certain tracks running along the other side of the road -- of the canyon. Were you aware of any means of travel along what we see as the right-hand side of the canyon by vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I don't remember the track on the right side. Maybe I did not pay attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, just so that we've got the position clear, is it that you really went there so infrequently at that time that you don't know one way or the other what was taking place along there?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: If you're referring to 1998 and 1999, I can frankly say that I was not there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. You can say, though, I think, is this correct, that even though you didn't observe the canal or its length at any point during that year, that you know that the water-flow was unusually high that year?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In order for you to better understand, there is a sketch of the catchment area in Decan, of the intake in Decan, where I mentioned that we could not manipulate with the three gates because they were fixed for a long time. And because the water flowed all the time, we did not know or we did not have the instrument to measure what water-flow there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, just bear with me for a moment. Leaving measurements aside, you have indicated, in the witness statement that you attested to this morning, that you do know that during 1998 there was more water than usual. You say you know that because there was an overflow in the lake, that there had been a lot of snow in the winter of 1997 to 1998, and that by June or July the overflow in the lake was 40 centimetres and the noise of the water so loud that people who were stationed there were unable to sleep. Now, that is a summary of what you say in paragraphs 38 and 84 of your witness statement. I'm paraphrasing. So can you confirm for us, please, that you were aware that the water levels were higher than in normal years?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- because we have a piece of equipment. Where the U014 is, there's the end of the lake and you can see the Bitesh hill. After, behind that lake, that hill is where the water overflows, and that indicated to us that there was an overflow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: But we did not have any information about the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. But the water that's coming into the lake is coming through the canal, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a 40-centimetre overflow in the lake would indicate a heavy flow in the canal, would it not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: There was a big inflow, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And that was the position throughout the summer?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've told us that you were not aware of Sali Zejnaj deliberately manipulating the gates to leave them up until June. But were you aware that when he left in June, he left the gates wide open at Lluka e Eperme?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I don't want to confuse things here. We are speaking about gates that take the water from the river and not gates that leave the river take its own natural course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that. The purpose of the gates is to divert the water from the River Bishtrica from the canal down into the lake. I think we all understand that. And when you leave the gates open into the canal, the effect is to divert the water from the river into the canal; is it not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've told us already that you were not aware of Mr. Zejnaj deliberately doing that in order to cause the River Bishtrica to be lower prior to June. I understand that. The question that I'm asking you is: Were you aware that when he left in June, he also left the gates open so that the River Bishtrica would be permanently diverted into the canal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm really confused here, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'd like to know is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we are talking about the gates, I'd like to know exactly what gates we are talking about. If I take you to the -- the annexes to the statement, if we look at annex 3, and perhaps the version as we find it in the statement at the original page 5, which is U0163144. Witness, if you could look at that as well, that is the marked sketch you made. I do understand that the natural flow of the river is in direction B and that what the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you excuse me for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about page 5 of the original, not of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The natural flow of water in the river is in direction B, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now there are gates indicated with A. I find those same gates in the original on page 7; that is, two gates, if I well understood. Picture on page 7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.
