utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I do understand if you open the gates, the water will take the natural flow through the river; whereas, if you close the gates, then the water will be diverted into the canal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Emmerson, may I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Can I explain a little bit something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only gate A suffices to be closed or opened, and this process happens. I'm speaking about the time then, what the situation was then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear to me. Mr. Emmerson, where I got confused --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is on page 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, 45 of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to leave them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "But are you aware that when he left in June, he left the gates wide open?" And then you said: "The purpose of the gates is -- and when you leave the gates open from the canal, the effect is to divert the water" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- "from the river to the ..." There it is really confusing for me.--

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It depends on which case we're referring to. I will clarify, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is a means by which the flow of water into the canal can be controlled with the system that appears in that diagram marked with C, D, E, and F, is there not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the more open the gates there are, the more water will flow into the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Yeah. [Interpretation] I will explain now. If you look at picture 63144 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- the gates C, D, and F were permanently open, not only during the war but even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: They were open and remained open until 2002 or 2003, as far as I remember. Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: With 1A or 2A, if you opened them, the water flows away; if you close them, the water flows into the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And the gates at D, E, and F, they're capable of being closed, aren't they? They can be closed?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, now, yes, but not then at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I think the witness testified - but I would have to find that - that these gates were not adjustable.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at the time. And, therefore, I was really confused which gates we were talking about because --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you are talking about manipulating gates, of which the witness earlier said that at that time through these gates you could not control the water-level in the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm seeking to clarify this witness's evidence in connection with the by the statements that have been made by the man who operated them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber is not aware of that, so we try to understand on the basis of what --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand entirely. Just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I then ask you, first of all, please, to look at the witness statement that was made by Sali Zejnaj to the Prosecution on the 8th of August of this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This was only served on us yesterday evening, so I'm afraid it was not loaded into the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent to us and I printed them out on last break, but I forgot to take them from my desk. So if there is any copy available --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, we have copies. There is an Albanian and an English copy for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, if I may, to look at two passages in this statement and then two passages in a statement this witness has made to the Defence. First of all, could you turn to paragraph 23 of Mr. Zejnaj's -- I'm sorry. You have in Albanian, Mr. Zejnaj's statement there, I think. If you could turn to paragraph 23, I'll just read it into the record. "Answering a question from the investigator, during the conflict I moved between Irzniq and Upper Lluka to check the intake about every three days. As far as I can remember, I went to the intake to open the gates to ease the flow of water in the River Bishtrica so that the people could cross the river easily. "The people wanted to cross the river, as it was dangerous for them to travel on the main roads as these were taken by the Serbs." And then he says: "The people were leaving the villages close to the main road like Baballoq, Gramaqel, Dubrava, Shaptej, and Gllogjan." And: "Had to cross the river so that they could reach the other side to villages Isniq, Prapaqan, Brelic, Kryshec, and Dubovik," because he says those were safer. "The area on this side of the river did not have the presence of Serb troops. And the question that arrises from that is that Mr. Zejnaj seems to be saying that in order to enable people to cross the River Bishtrica, he was reducing the flow of water by manipulating the gates at Lluka e Eperme. But he describes it as opening the gates to ease the flow so that people could cross the river easily. I wonder if you could help us with what he is referring to there.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: He has stated here exactly what happened and how it was. If you have the map of the intake --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- you will see that after the intake, there is a part of the river where you can cross the river. I will explain. In order for people to be able to cross the river, at the end of this intake, he deviated the water towards the canal and offered the possibility to people to cross the river, but this is at the end of the intake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the effect of what he is doing is to divert the flow of water from the river and into the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, that's how you do it. That's the function.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he describes that as opening the gates. Do you know why that is?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Maybe there's a misunderstanding of what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Maybe in translation there was something that was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- wrongly understood. If you open A, the water flows its course; if you close it, it deviates.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now then let me put the question to you again that I put earlier. Did you know that he was deviating the water from the river into the canal? However that's mechanically achieved, did you know that that's what he was doing in order to let people cross?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I did not have any contact with him, so how could I have known?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. But the effect of doing that in this year where the water-levels were unusually high would be to increase the flow of water in the canal, would it not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Can I add something? Maybe it's difficult for you to understand. But if we refer to the photograph on page 5, point A on the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- has a function to deplete the water that is in the -- in the intake area. There's a photograph on page 6 as well, which shows the direction of the water-flow. If you open point A, the water is depleted completely from here. If you open the right gate, the water is not completely depleted, and that's how he could manipulate with it, whether he could send more or less water to the canal. This is technically how it functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for that explanation. If we could just drop down to paragraph 30 in his witness statement, he says this - and for the record I'll read it - "Answering a question from the investigator, if a body is dropped in the canal, the current is so forceful that it can transport objects even heavier than dead bodies will flow all the way to the beginning of the lake. They will cross the canyon as well. "The height of water in the channel at the beginning of the channel is 70 centimetres, if the flow is 12 metres cubed per second opinion. The channel is roughly two metres deep. The canyon will be even less deep as it is wider." Now, Mr. Zejnaj obviously had greater practical opportunity day-to-day opportunity to observe the canal in 1998 than you did. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. He could observe until June, but I don't know how often. As I said earlier, I'm not his line manager -- I was not his line manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. But if we look at the passage that we've just looked at in paragraph 23, he says he was moving between Irzniq and Upper Lluka, at least, every three days until the conflict when he left in June. So I just want to be clear, would you agree with his assessment that if the current is in the canal, perhaps especially in a year of heavy flow where the water is being deliberately manipulated in this way, that it could be so forceful that it could transmit objects even heavier than a dead body all the way along the canal and to the opening of the lake. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I can agree with one thing, that everything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The fact itself -- I don't know whether you know what 12 cubic metres per second means. It's such a force that creates -- it creates a canyon. I don't know what actually happened there. Sali might have been there more often than me. Of course he was, and what he says may be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that is the usual -- roughly the usual maximum flow, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The annual average is two to three cubic metres per second, but sometimes there are 12, 10 cubic metres, sometimes one or two cubic metres, but this is not relevant. So the amount that enters the canal does not -- is not an indicator what the level of the lake is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I understand. If you listen to my question, perhaps I should put it to you again. The figure that Mr. Zejnaj gives in his witness statement of 12 cubic metres per second, that would ordinarily, in ordinary circumstances, that would be the strongest or maximum flow in the canal, would it not?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If the canal was fully utilised by a heavy flow from the River Bishtrica diverted into the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The canal is never full because the speed is very high and the energy of the water is very high.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think there may have been a translation error there. Just to be absolutely clear, that figure of 12 cubic metres would be the normal maximum when there was no obstruction at Lluka e Eperme preventing water from entering the canal and when the gates were closed to prevent the water from flowing into the River Bishtrica. That would be the maximum flow when the water in the canal was at its heaviest?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The largest amount of water is 12 cubic metres per second.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] "Per second," I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Since the witness is taking us to page 6, could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ask you to go back to page 5 in the original, and could you tell us, you indicated something with a G there which is not explained in your statement. Could you tell us what you indicated by the letter G.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not -- [Interpretation] I don't see it, the G that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's your sketch, your sketch, left from the sketch, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's C, that is not G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I see a G just at the border. I see a C where the river flows, that's under the B. But what looks like a G and is different from another C, I see -- Mr. Dutertre, could you assist me. Do we all see a G there or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that there is a reference to G in paragraph 16, which is where the statement was made, or rather, where the photograph that follows was taken. G is where the photograph was taken. At the beginning of paragraph 7, there is mention of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. [In English] Objection. I'm sorry. [Interpretation] G is interpreted like this. It corresponds to another photograph that is connected with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I now see in 16. Yes, yes. I now -- yes. I was not looking -- I was not looking well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The explanation is given in relation to the photograph. Yes, it's clear. It's perfectly clear. I would have one other question in this respect. If you look at how that photograph is taken on page 6, it looks as if there's some kind of overflow next to the gate. You see the first long line on the left of the photograph. Could you explain to me what that is. That is -- it looks like concrete and that's where the tire is close to. Is that a kind of a safety overflow facility? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The G letter you mentioned earlier corresponds to the photo on page 6 from where the photo was taken. Now D is linked with D, E, F on page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for a second, because I have got no problems at all to understand now both G and the whole sketch. I think at least I do understand. What I'm interested to know is on the photograph on page 6, we see there is water to the right. At the back, we have the -- the entry into the canal. On the left back, we have the gate which allows the water to flow or to continue to flow in the river. Now, I see a concrete structure which go from the left, bottom-top of the photograph to approximately two-thirds, just slightly to the right upwards, which is rather light on the photograph and which appears, at first sight to me, to be a kind of a concrete structure. And I wonder what the function of that is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concrete structure is used to help accumulate the water on point B, and the water is collected there; and then you see in letter -- on letter E, its direction for the canal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if the water -- is there so much water that the canal cannot take it? And if you close the gates at A, what would happen with the remainder of the water? Would that flow over what here seems to be a -- I hardly dare to use the word dam, which it seems to be. Would it flow over that dam and continue its natural force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right. That's exactly how it is. This is the place from where the surplus amount of water goes out. The excess water which the canal cannot contain goes over this concrete structure and flows naturally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is on the basis of this structure that you could tell us what the maximum flow of water in the canal is. Because if there would be more, it would just flow into the river because the canal cannot take it, the water-level would rise, and then flow over the dam. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very correctly understood. If there is more than 12 cubic metres, then it goes on this side over the structure. The canal can contain only up to 12 cubic metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier a worker at Lluka e Eperme who'd worked with Mr. Zejnaj who was killed, Musli Mulliqi. First of all, can I ask you to confirm that Mr. Mulliqi was shot by Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: First, I would kindly ask you to say Musli Mulliqi, which is his correct name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise for my pronunciation. Can you confirm that he was shot by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you confirm, please, that he was shot by the canal as he was leaving from work?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I had already made a remark; namely, that he was killed in the line of duty when he was performing his job --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- because he was near his house, and the canal from his house to the canal is very near.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, just so that we're clear, he lived in property owned by the company, which was situated adjacent to the canal and close to Lluka e Eperme, to the intake point?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. At the intake point was that little house which we repaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come to that in a little while. But he was shot, was he not, as he was walking along the edge of the canal by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Our tradition is to go to the house of the deceased and pay your condolences, so this is what we did and this is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: We felt it our moral obligation to go to his family and pay a visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us with anything more specific. How far along the canal section from the intake point was he shot dead, roughly? Can you give us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Maybe 100, 150 metres. But you must know that he was responsible not only for the intake point but also for the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, when we ask a witness for an estimate, then it's usually an estimate based on what he saw or what he was told --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in further detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got no idea who told him this. I don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the witness has said the information, so far he has said, the source of the information came from the family when he visited them immediately after, so I was about to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether the family saw it and the whether assessment is an assessment by the family or him being shown certain areas and then make his own assessment as far as distances are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I entirely take the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you please try and remember as much as possible of what you were told and by whom you were told about the circumstances and location of this fatal shooting?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: When we went to his house to pay our condolences, we saw the police forces in front of the door. We did our visit and asked what happened, and they told us approximately the place where he was shot. And based on their words, I gave this rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. These were police forces of the MUP, were they?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did they tell you they'd shot him because they'd thought he was in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is "they" the family or the police?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. They, the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. That was unclear from the previous question when the witness said "they told me" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- he had referred to both family and friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did the police tell you they shot your colleague because they believed him to be in the KLA? Is that what they told you?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No. We didn't talk with them, frankly speaking, but we learned this information from another source. We didn't talk with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I thought you told us a moment ago, but perhaps you can help us with some clarity on this. I thought you told us --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The family members --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think he's referring to where I made the observation that the day was unclear, whether that was police or family.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us that when you went to his house to pay condolences, you saw police forces in front of the door. You asked what had happened, and they told you approximately the place where he was shot. Now, could you tell us who it was who told you the place where he was shot.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: We were told by the family members in the room where we were expressing our condolences, where people had gathered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, do you know how they knew where he had been shot?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: It's my guess - it's not that I am certain - but I suppose they were the ones who got his corpse.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And were you told that he had been travelling in a car at that time?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No, that's not true that he was travelling in a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. The information you received was that he was walking. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The distance from his home to the place didn't need to use a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can I ask you this: Do you know when in -- this shooting occurred?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I don't know for sure. I gave this information when I was asked to make a statement, and when we could look at the archives of the enterprise --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- which certified the time that the deceased died.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for helping us as much as you can. Can I ask, please, that you be shown a further statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps one follow-up. You say you don't know when. Have you got no idea. Was it 1997? 2000? 1998? Was it summer? Was it autumn? Do you remember the circumstances under which you visited the family, for example? Was that during the war? Before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was for sure before 1999. Of this I'm sure, but I'm not so certain whether it was 1997 or 1998. A long time has passed. I only know that it was bad weather. It was raining when we went to see him. Maybe it's a mistake there. I wouldn't dare manipulate with the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to follow-up on that, I asked you a question a little earlier on about whether you learned that he had been shot in the mistaken belief that he was a member of the KLA. And I haven't got the transcript reference in front of me, but my recollection was that you replied that you learned that from somewhere else. Can I ask you: Was he killed during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: You asked me how I found out about that. We were informed by the directorate of the company that he was killed. That's why we went to pay him a visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. I'm sorry. Did the director of the company inform you that there was a belief that he'd been killed because he was suspected to be a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Maybe it's not good of me to say this, but do you know who the director was? You cannot expect him to say this. I might have been in his place --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- and he would have described the event in the same way.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I regret to respond in this way, but, of course, he wouldn't admit to him being killed by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand why you say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, perhaps it doesn't take us much further on --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- this matter. I just want to say one word when I asked you that you believed he was killed as a mistaken belief. I don't think "mistaken" was part of the question, and at the same time I don't think the witness could answer that question, if put that way, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave the question there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask that you be shown a statement made by Sali Zejnaj to the Defence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would need a number, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the other -- oh, yes, the other statement, the statement of Sali Zejnaj, you have read from it. Is it your intention to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then first now the statement of Zejnaj -- Sali Zejnaj needs a number, that's interview dated 8th of August, 2006. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D121, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We have -- yes, this is the English version or does there exist any Albanian version of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There doesn't, I'm afraid. I was going to ask the witness whether or not he reads English; if not, to take him through the passages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm still talking about Sali Zejnaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh, yes, there does. For a Prosecution statement there does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. Now we have the statement taken by the Defence from Sali Zejnaj. That would be, Mr. Registrar, number ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that is in the system at 1D45-0038.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you take proper care that when putting passages to the witness that there is no Albanian original.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll speak at an appropriate speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be clear whether you are able to speak -- I'm sorry, to read any English?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you can read in English?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, if we can look at the second paragraph on the first page beginning for the first month, it reads: "For the first month, I was working as a security worker, and after that I became dam manipulator in the village Lluka e Eperme, where I am still working at present." I just draw attention to that at present, because when, in this statement, when the word "dam" appears, it's a reference to the intake facility at Lluka e Eperme. I wonder, first of all, if you can turn to page 2, in this statement, to the fourth line down, where there is a reference to the death of Musli Mulliqi, and you can see that a date there is given for his death having being killed by Serbian forces in September 1998. I take it that you're not in a position one way or the other to confirm or contradict that?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No. I can confirm this because this is the very reason that his son continues to work with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But in relation to the date, I thought your evidence a moment ago was that you simply couldn't remember one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours please, he could. He could remember that it was late 1997 or early 1998. I think that's what he said in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From what I remember is that he said that it would not be 1999. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, definitely not 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought he referred to early 1998, but 1997 or 1998, because otherwise there would be a contradiction if it would be early 1998 with this statement. I'll find it for you and then see if my recollection is right. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My recollection, for what it is worth, is that the witness wasn't able to say whether for sure it was during the conflict or not, which is why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. He said not 1999. We can all look it up, and then we know what the witness said. If that needs any further comment, then we will hear from you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you need, I can repeat what I said. I cannot remember accurately when.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If I can just pick up on page 3, there's two passages I want to take you to first of all. And once I've gone through them with you, I would like to ask you to comment on them. First of all, the third full paragraph on page 3 for the record reads: "I remember that in March 1998, the situation became very tense around the villages where I was working. The danger was that sometimes there was shooting between the Serbian and UCK soldiers. Both forces had positions in the area of the dam, but neither directly controlled the dam. I had to continue to work because someone had to stay at the dam to control the water-flow and also at the same time I needed money." And then picking it up in the paragraph at the bottom of that page: "During that period from March 1998 to September 1998, the dam was in the firing line between the two forces and wasn't controlled by anyone. Serbian forces were moving sometimes closer to shoot at KLA soldiers. The KLA soldiers were coming with me when I was going to the dam, giving me protection so that I could carry on operating the water controls and carry out the cleaning of the filters for the canal. "Above the dam, in the direction of Gjakove, the distance of Serbian forces was around a thousand metres left from the dam. This is looking to the main road that goes to Gjakove. Approximately, 600 metres below the dam, there were KLA/UCK soldiers. They were not in any particular fixed positions that I could see. I never saw the KLA soldiers move closer to the dam. "The Serbian forces were moving closer to the dam, shooting in different areas, including our work-place. I recognised them as Serbian forces because they were coming armed with tanks and heavy weapons." So pausing there for a moment, were you aware that there was fighting going on between the two sides in the immediate vicinity of the dam at Lluka e Eperme between March and September?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Are you asking me whether I was present there or whether I heard of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whether you heard of it. I appreciate you weren't present because you've already told us that.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us where you heard of it from and how you learnt of it?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In Gjakove, there was the Office for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms. And very often we contacted that office to get information on what was going on, where the war was being waged, where there were problems in order to avoid contact with the problematic areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I just wanted to tell you that in this office, this Council for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms, you may find the statement of the position of the Serb forces. When they were shelling the dam -- from the dam, we asked them to leave the place because we were afraid that the dam would suffer some damage because of the great detonations and explosions, and you have information to that effect I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've got about another 20 minutes or so for this witness. I'm entirely in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the indication was that you needed one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I know, and I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, on the basis of how matters stand now, how much time do you think you would need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very difficult to valuate because we haven't had the full cross-examination, but I would think about 20 minutes on the basis of what Mr. Emmerson has already done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course I asked you first because in the present situation you do not know yet what the cross-examination of the other counsel would be. Mr. Guy-Smith, how much do you think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Depending on how things go, about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I don't anticipate any cross-examination of this witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. If we have a break now, we would resume at five minutes to 1.00. 20 minutes would bring us to quarter past 1.00. Mr. Guy-Smith, you said 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seven minutes, that would bring us to -- yes. Mr. Emmerson, we will have a break now; upon resuming, you'll have until 12 minutes past 1.00, that's a little bit shorter than you indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have your seven minutes, Mr. Guy-Smith. And then you should finish before quarter to 2.00. We stand adjourned and we'll resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed. At the same time, I have for the end of this session a few procedural matters which I think I can handle in seven minutes. So if everyone could save - not you, Mr. Guy-Smith - if everyone could save a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will be shorter based on my conversation with Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, if I may, just to deal with one or two other issues in Mr. Zejnaj's witness statement. First of all, page 5, the second main paragraph, I won't read it out because time is pressing, he indicates that the level of water was very high at the dam during this period, and that as a result he had with the other workers there to cut the dam filters off because there was a possibility that they would be blocked by rubbish. And says: "After we cut the filters off, I opened the water-control gates for the canal to send most of the water down the canal. Water flowed through the Radoniq Lake at a very high level. This was recorded on my reports of the water-level." Question for you: Were you aware that he had cut the filters off?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I don't know what he meant when he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Did you find any damage to the filters yourself at any time?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Many of the bars were not touched. I think he meant those, the bars. Maybe not at all touched.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Probably one or two bars may have been damaged, but 95 per cent of them were in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Moving to the following paragraph, he indicates that at the end of June, when the situation became tense and Serbian forces were within 300 metres of the dam, he left the area and didn't go back until June 1999. And he says: "That day," this is a quotation. "That day, when I left the dam, the gates of dam were opened to the maximum that water can flow to the Radoniq canal and not the Bishtrica River. (The gates of Bishtrica River were closed so that a minimum flowed into the river)." Again, does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Can you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. He says, if you can look at the last four lines of the second or the third full paragraph on page 5, the paragraph that begins: "At the end of June," Mr. Zejnaj indicates when he left the dam, he says: "The gates were open to the maximum that water can flow to the Radoniq canal and not to the Bishtrica River. (The gates of Bishtrica River were closed so a minimum of water flowed into the river)." The question I'm asking you is does that assist in your recollection as to the way in which the matter -- the gates had been left, the configuration had been left in June?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is Mr. Emmerson asking was that the situation when this witness went back some time later?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think Mr. Emmerson is asking whether the witness has any recollection of how the dam was left in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whether the witness was aware, is the question that I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, was aware, because I think the witness earlier testified that he had not been there earlier in June. Do you have any information as to how the dam was left in June 1998?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any information as to how the dam was left in June 1998, but this is in conformity with my statement. Otherwise, the water would not have flown to the lake. That's why I think he must have left the gates like that. I said that water came during the summertime, and that's why I say that it's the same as I said in my statement. How did I know that the water went into the lake? Because the level rose.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And just follow-up on that. Normally, during the summer, the configuration at the lot would be left so that for the summer months, there was no water flowing through the canal; is that correct? That would be the normal thing in normal years?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In normal times, there are two or three indications that changed the whole system, because there is the water in the reservoir in Decan, then the water that flows until the Bishtrica River, which has to be left -- some kind of amount of water has to be left this, and then the water that we divert to the Radoniq Lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you turn to page 6 now, where we can see - and I'll summarize it for you, again because time is pressing - that Mr. Zejnaj indicates that in June 1999 when he returned to the area, there was a first clean-up operation. And he refers to a clean-up operation that began in the area around the police station at Irzniq in which he indicates that in June 1999 two dead bodies were recovered, one of which was identified as a man called Daut Aliqkaj, and that he learned from people in the village that this man's wife had been present when he was killed by the Serbs. Can I ask you: Were you aware that the body of a man who was believed to have been killed by the Serbs had been recovered in the canal close to Irzniq police station in June 1999?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about any bodies there. I was not aware of any bodies or of anything that happened in the lake or in the canal. I've seen bodies elsewhere. I was not asked about those, and I did not give a statement about those. So I saw bodies on the terrain somewhere else, but not on the canal -- in the canal and in Radoniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Final question, if I may, because of the time. You mentioned an occasion when you thought you may be required to close the gates during the Serbian investigation of the canal in which bodies are recorded as having been found. And we discussed earlier on whether that was in August or in September. I just want to ask you this: We have records indicating that the Serb authorities arranged for a Serbian employee of the company to close the gates so as to divert the water away from the canal and into the Bishtrica River on the 9th of September, and I just want to understand this: If that were done and if it were then to rain, where would the water-flow? Into the Bishtrica River or into the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: If the gates are closed in a direction of the river and if there is rain over 15 cubic metres, then it goes towards the river; if it's less, then it goes towards the canal. When you asked me about the intervention and the investigation, when we were asked to do that, we were escorted by a police car and we were told to go and stop the water in the canal in Decan because Lluka e Eperme is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: During that time, we were not allowed to go there, so a Serb person was asked to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause there. If the configuration at Lluka e Eperme is organised so that the water supplied to the canal is shut off, if that occurs and then it rains, will the flow -- will there be a flow of water in the canal or will there be a flow of water in the river or both?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Without taking into account whether the gates are closed or open, the water can flow into both.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But if the gates to the river have been left open --

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] Open.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the gates to the river have been left open so as to divert the flow of water away from the canal and it subsequently rains, my question is: Would there then be a torrent of water in the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Part of the amount of water could go into the canal if it rains heavily.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. We're facing here the same gates, open/gates closed. I referred to that earlier. I haven't seen the records, so I can't interpret them. The only thing I'd like to do is tell you that I identified page 12, line 18, as the one where the impossibility to manipulate the gates until 2003 was mentioned by the witness. Mr. Guy-Smith -- and at the same time I'd like to give one comment on rain. Rain drops everywhere. So whether there's a flow, it depends what rain what you're talking about. Of course, water that drops into the canal itself certainly will find its way into the stream. Therefore, If heavy rain, we all know there will be a stream. The question was not all that clear, but let's first see whether Mr. Guy-Smith has further questions for the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do. Neither about the rain or the plain or in Spain. I have no question about any of those things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, I want to make sure I understand one aspect of your evidence correctly, which deals with the issue of the maintenance workers who were at the canal. Those were two individuals, if I understood your testimony correctly. One was a gentleman by the name of Sali Zejnaj. The other was a gentleman by the name of Musli Mulliqi; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, but they were not aware of what was going on, and, in fact, they did not report on things. They just kept notes in a notebook, and their house was burned down, so the notes were lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Their direct boss was a gentleman by the name of Xheton Shasivari; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Jeton.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise. Jeton Shasivari?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. True.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, when Mr. Mulliqi was shot and killed, at the same time, his son was also wounded, wasn't he? He was shot, I think, in the stomach and in the leg; right?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I heard something about this, but I do not have hundred per cent correct information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you said you heard something about this, is this something that you heard about from the family when you went to go visit the family because of Mr. Mulliqi's death?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No. We heard about Mr. Mulliqi and about all this in Gjakove, because the information came up to us, to the office where our office -- where our directorate is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So, as you sit here today, you can't tell us where you had heard that Mr. Mulliqi's son had also been shot at the time that he had been killed, but you have a memory that you'd heard that information. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I just heard of it; but from whom and when, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you hear that at that time that Mr. Mulliqi was shot and killed, that the shots had come from a Serbian armoured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Look, we did not enter into such analysis. We just felt sorry for the family and the person who died. That's it. We just heard that he was killed, and that's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One more question with regard to the circumstances of his death. Did you hear any information from the family or from any other individual that you could identify that the reason that he was killed was because the Serbian police thought that he was driving a car owned by the KLA? And if you did hear that, fine; if you didn't hear that, so be it.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I know he was killed. And in this misfortune, the good thing is that, well, I might have been killed, too, and they might have labelled me as a member of the KLA or attributed something else to me. At the beginning, I said I don't like to speak about things that I don't have arguments about or just to base my judgements on hearsay. I know that the person was killed by the Serbs. As to what they attributed to him, this is something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's one other matter that I'd like to ask you about. Once again, I'm dealing with the subject of cars, and I'm referring to your statement. You learned from Mr. Zejnaj that during, the war the MUP police confiscated local people's cars and dumped them into the canal at different places, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: That is correct. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Well, apparently I'm not done.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you wish me to say something else in response to your question -- in response to your question, it is true that I was at the site of the event with the investigators. And to tell you the truth, I was rather angry with this person because I asked him, "Why didn't you take immediate photos of the situation?" But maybe the conditions were such that he couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that you were asking the investigator to take immediate photos of the situation, what investigator was that? Who was that person?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Not the investigator, but Sali Zejnaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. Did you receive any information from Sali Zejnaj about where the cars were dumped by the Serbian police into the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: According to his statement, he was -- he visited several parts of the canal and he saw them in -- dumped in several areas. I'm talking about various distances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "the canal," using the terminology that we've used here today, you're referring to the natural part of the canyon that flows after the concrete part all the way to the lake; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: We are talking only about that part of the canal that is concrete. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harvey, you haven't changed your mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Still no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still no questions. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to be as brief as possible, first of all. And I would like to apologise ahead of time because I'm lagging slightly behind. I would like to apologise the statement of Sali Zejnaj that was presented. I wanted to have a French translation -- I was waiting for the French translation. I was not able to intervene at the right moment. I don't know whether this should be under 92 bis or 92 ter, but I want this statement to be put into the file so that it -- so that the Prosecutor can cross-examine Sali Zejnaj. Now, I believe this will be a witness called by the Defence, and perhaps we can reserve this question of this document and just give it an identification number at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, you would like to have the -- we have now two statements. One has already D121, and the other one is D122. So, therefore, whether it could be used as 92 bis or 92 ter depends on the -- whether all the requirements are met. At the same time, of course, they are now admitted into evidence for the limited purposes of having reference to the context of a statement of a witness. Whether the Defence wants or doesn't want to call the witness is not known to me, but let's not at this moment spend too much time on this. And let's see whether you have any further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I do have additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 29 of today's transcript, Mr. Emmerson asked you whether you could help us as regards the undergrowth in the canal in 1998. We're referring here to the part of the canal that is near Irzniq, and you said no. My question is as follows: You went to the canal in 2002 when the cleaning operation began. Could you tell us what the average diameter of the trees were that were extracted from the canal when you went there in 2002?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: On page 28 of the annex, you find my description of the undergrowth, how big their diameter of the trees was, and you could see also the photos produced after the cleaning took place. I wanted to make a clear description of the part near the Irzniq police station, why that part was not cleaned for a long time, and you have an explanation for that. I also wanted to explain that it was very dense, that area, in undergrowth, even though the canal is very wide. For me, it seems strange why it was in that state, whether the bodies could pass through or could remain there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sefa. As regards the flow rate of the canal, you mentioned 12 cubic metres on the average. What is the average -- what is the average annual flow of the canal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't that in the statement of the witness, Mr. Dutertre? And is there any question in cross-examination that triggered this question? Number 36, the average flow and river -- no, that is the river. "The average flow of the canal is two to three cubic metres per second but it depends on the flow of water in Bishtrica." So that gives an answer to the question, doesn't it. So why put again the same question, unless there is any reason you would like to give it some other follow-up. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have here the word "average." [In English] "Average," [Interpretation] which is two to three. [In English] Maximum is 12 to 15. Depends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is clear. I was just asking Mr. Dutertre whether that question had to be put for a second time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, we know that the canal and the Radoniq Lake is -- well, the water comes from the canal. Are there other sources of water, other than rain-water, of course? Are there other streams or other sources of water that flow into that lake?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Yes. You can find that information in map number 163279 [as interpreted], addendum 25, where I described the flow of the water before the lake was built. The flow estimated was one cubic at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sefa. Do you know about Mr. Sali Zejnaj's qualifications in hydrology? What degrees he may have?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: Sali Zejnaj had finished the high school, but we had another system in place. At the intake point, he should mark only the level of the water of the canal in centimetres, and then we transformed that into water quantity. It's a simple method of calculating the water quantity, and he did a routine job. Whether it was ten centimetres high, it meant such-and-such cubics.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. I'd like to go on to another question. Mr. Guy-Smith asked you a question about the Serb authorities and the Serb police having put -- thrown cars into the canal. Do you know at what point in time that occurred?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: In my statement, I have declared that I learned this information on the day that we made a site visit in Irzniq when we observed the terrain. That day he mentioned the number 300 or 400 cars, and I said, "That seems to be quite a large number and that you haven't counted them. So you might as well just mention that there were a number of cars there." So that was a first time for me to learn of this fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: But did you hear about when, what point in time, these Serb police had put these cars into the canal?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No. I had no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre. Judge Hoepfel has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Sefa, you made a short statement today. I quote: "I was not aware of any bodies or of anything that happened in the lake or in the canal. I've seen bodies elsewhere. I was not asked about those and I didn't give a statement about those. So I saw bodies on the terrain somewhere else, but not on the canal, in the canal or in Radoniq," meaning the lake, probably. Can you explain to us a little more about that? What have you seen?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: It is, I'll say, a difficult and at the same time a sad question, because during the war we were a team that worked together, irrespective of the qualifications we had. Once, in Gjakove, we had to go to cut the water supply. And, unfortunately, I have to say, that we tread on some corpses. It was wartime and we didn't know where to turn to provide the information, but people knew about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: When was that about?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I mean 7, 8, 9 of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And what happened later after that?

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: What could happen? We continued our work. We told each other not to say a word about what we saw, because we were afraid that someone might kill us if they knew that we had learned of that fact. There was no place we could go to complain about that. We didn't know what to do with this information. That was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [In English] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have also one question for you. If you please look at annex 27 -- no, not 27. 28, please. That's a sketch you apparently made.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the sketch, I find some debris at the bottom, and I find that you have drawn vegetation vertically just growing up, if I read it well, four to five metres from the bottom. Could you tell me when you saw the canal, did you see any trees or trunks which were horizontally in the canal? So I'm trying to find out whether there were any trees cut and thrown into the canal where you would expect them to be more or less horizontally, or whether you only found trees or bushes in the position as you have included in your sketch.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: The sketch I have drawn is to give you an idea of the terrain at that point and why it was not cleaned. If you look at annex 22, you'll note that near the trunk that you see in this photo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: -- and annex 21 as well, you'll see the vegetation and why in the main sketch you cannot see the canal as drawn. The auto photo, it said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether your answer is entirely clear to me. I see that it was not cleaned. But referring to your sketch in which you put some debris on the bottom, but vegetation only vertically that seems as if it has grown there, I wonder whether there was any vegetation such as trunks of trees or thicker bushes which apparently had not grown there but had been thrown in there. If you don't know, then ...

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: I don't think that someone threw them there. They grew of themselves. It's a natural growth of vegetation that took place there. In my statement, I've already pointed out that because of the positioning of the Serbian police forces which were stationed some ten metres away, we were unable to clean that part, that section of the canal. You may look at the photo yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear to me, but what you saw was natural growth rather than trunks of trees or bushes, thicker bushes, to be thrown into the water.

utterances.speaker: FATON SEFA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions, then I would like to thank you very much, Mr. Sefa, for coming to The Hague, for answering all the questions put to you by the parties and the Bench. And I would like to wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, can you please assist the witness out of the courtroom so we can deal with a few procedural matters for the remaining seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, when the witness spoke, he expressed thanks to everyone in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's deal with a few procedural matters. I'd like to go into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there are any other remarks on the revised witness list by the Defence, the Chamber would like to be informed as soon as possible. Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, you announced that, in relation to Exhibits D56, 58, and 59, that you would inform the Trial Chamber that the Prosecution will not oppose admission, but there would be several reservations to be made. I don't know. If you could do that in half a minute, I would invite you to do that now; if not, the Chamber would like to hear from you as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can't do that now, Your Honours, at least in a considered fashion, but I would need some time and I will look into that and provide an answer to that as swiftly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. And we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the semi-last issue you raised, where you would like to respond to a subpoena request, would it be possible that you -- yes, I'm not going into any further detail. Could you do that by --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We could do it by Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By Monday, that's fine. Finally, you asked -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm just raising this for the purpose of discussion. If there's any further material arising from the comment that Your Honours extracted from the lady's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- e-mail, I'm sure the Defence probably -- and we provide that, I'm sure that the Defence will probably want to digest -- look at that at least before saying anything about the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the earlier your provided that --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I understand that. But I am just saying that the Defence would probably want to put off making any submissions until they have had a chance to look at that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it the Defence is in the expectation that they will receive that material not later than Friday, close of business.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll see how that develops. Then, finally, you asked, Mr. Emmerson, in private session, and as you rightly said was not done in private session, for five minutes to address a general issue on the testimony of the witness whose testimony we heard today. You'll be given an opportunity to do that for five minutes. Please think it over to what extent what you are going to say is not already on our minds. That is opinion evidence. The Chamber is well aware of what is opinion and what is facts, and usually takes already into account that opinion is not primarily to be given by a witness of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have a reason for raising it. I will deal with it if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have five minutes. Then we will, with apologises to interpreters, transcriber, technicians, security, for being seven minutes late, we'll adjourn to Monday, the 25th of June, Courtroom I, quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
